resolutions.reproduced: Yes, all four, against copies of the real app.py/index.html: (a) server reads excludeBoilerplate -> 0 failures; (b) UI hardcodes exclude_boilerplate: true -> 0; (c) upload handler compares == "true" -> 0; (d) extract_items(path, exclude_boilerplate=not exclude_boilerplate) -> 0. resolutions.option_taken: BINDING, not HTTP. The HTTP alternative was reconsidered on the orchestrator's guidance and rejected on a mechanical fact rather than a preference: evals/run.py has no skip state — `score = passed / len(results)` over a bool — so a fastapi-dependent case is either silently green when the dependency is absent (forbidden, and the ADR-010 sin again) or red in three CI jobs that install nothing by ADR-003, which is a hard dependency in the gate. Giving the harness a skip state is a change to the gate mechanism for one case.
resolutions.fix: src/repo_hygiene/eval_adapter.py::check_boilerplate_plumbing rewritten to bind the two ends to each other instead of asking each end whether it mentions the flag. Per input mode it derives the literals the UI puts on the wire (the JSON key paired with excludeBp(), or the `&key=value` it appends) and the literals the handler reads out of the request, and requires the two sets to be EQUAL; it requires every call site to read excludeBp() rather than a constant; and it requires the final hop to forward the parameter unmodified (`extract_items(path, exclude_boilerplate=exclude_boilerplate)`, which also rejects the older `extract_items(path)`).
resolutions.second_defect_found: Re-applying shape (b) to the REWRITTEN check found a second defect in the check itself: the flat 400-character call-site window ran into the next `$("#go-…")` handler, so a call site that hardcoded the value still found a neighbour's excludeBp() and passed. The window is now bounded by the next handler or endpoint literal. Found only because every shape was re-run after the rewrite instead of being assumed covered.
